about: The licence of each model under test, as its publisher states it. For open-weight models: the licence field of the model's card on Hugging Face (its API, https://huggingface.co/api/models/<id>) and, where the card says more, the card's own sentence. 'allows' is our short reading of the licence named, not legal advice: the linked text decides. Commercial models publish no weights; they are used under their provider's terms.

apache-2.0.name: Apache License 2.0
apache-2.0.allows: Use, change and redistribute the weights, commercially too, keeping the licence and notices; it carries a patent grant; no warranty. A standard open-source licence.

mit.name: MIT License
mit.allows: Use, change and redistribute the weights, commercially too, keeping the copyright and licence notice; no warranty. A standard open-source licence.

gemma.name: Gemma Terms of Use (Google's own terms)
gemma.allows: Not a standard open-source licence: Google's own terms, with a prohibited-use policy; the card is gated (the terms are accepted before download). We read the card's licence tag only, not the terms: read them before relying on this model beyond a test through an API.

llama4.name: Llama 4 Community License (Meta's own terms)
llama4.allows: Not a standard open-source licence: Meta's own community licence, with an acceptable-use policy; the card is gated (the terms are accepted before download, and we could not read the card without accepting them). We read the licence tag only: read the terms before relying on this model beyond a test through an API.

mistral-ecosystem.name: Mistral Ecosystem Open-Weight License
mistral-ecosystem.allows: The card's own words: 'a modified version of the MIT license, for both commercial and non-commercial use'; it adds that operating a model-as-a-service business needs a separate agreement. We read the card's sentence, not the licence text.
